questions.question_text: What is the main purpose of enterprise performance management (EPM) software?

options.A: To support planning, budgeting, forecasting, consolidation and performance reporting across the organization
options.B: To process day-to-day sales and purchase transactions
options.C: To manage network security and user passwords
options.D: To replace the external audit of financial statements

questions.explanation: EPM (also called corporate performance management) systems sit on top of transactional systems and help management plan, budget, forecast, consolidate results, model scenarios and monitor performance against strategy.

questions.question_text: In the systems development life cycle (SDLC), during which phase are user requirements gathered and the current system studied in detail?

options.C: Post-implementation review
options.D: Systems analysis

questions.explanation: In the systems analysis phase, analysts study the existing system and define user requirements for the new one. Design follows, then development and testing, implementation (including conversion and training), and ongoing operation and maintenance.

questions.question_text: Which task is the best candidate for robotic process automation (RPA)?

options.A: Deciding whether to enter a new geographic market
options.B: Copying data from standardized supplier invoices into the payables system using fixed rules
options.C: Negotiating a new labor agreement with a union
options.D: Assessing the reasonableness of management's goodwill impairment judgments

questions.explanation: RPA software bots mimic human actions in repetitive, high-volume, rule-based tasks with structured digital inputs. Strategic decisions, negotiations and complex judgments require human reasoning and are not suitable for RPA.

questions.question_text: A company subscribes to a web-based accounting application that the provider hosts, maintains and upgrades; users simply log in through a browser. Which cloud service model is this?

options.C: Software as a service (SaaS)
options.D: On-premises licensed software

questions.explanation: With SaaS, the provider delivers a complete application over the internet and manages the underlying infrastructure and software. IaaS provides only computing resources such as servers and storage, and PaaS provides a platform on which customers build and run their own applications.

questions.question_text: Which feature of blockchain technology is most relevant to the reliability of accounting records?

options.A: A single central administrator can edit any past transaction at will
options.B: Transactions are recorded on a distributed ledger, and once validated, blocks are extremely difficult to alter without detection
options.C: Transactions are stored only on the company's own server
options.D: Blockchain eliminates the need to verify the existence of the underlying assets

questions.explanation: Blockchain maintains a shared, distributed ledger in which each block is cryptographically linked to the previous one, making recorded transactions effectively immutable. However, it does not guarantee that the underlying transaction was valid or that the assets exist.

questions.question_text: An employee receives an email that appears to come from the company's bank, asking her to click a link and confirm her login credentials. This is an example of:

options.C: A brute-force password attack
options.D: Phishing

questions.explanation: Phishing uses fraudulent messages that impersonate trusted organizations to trick users into revealing credentials or other sensitive information. A denial-of-service attack floods a system with traffic, and brute-force attacks try many passwords.

questions.question_text: Malicious software encrypts a company's files and the attackers demand payment in cryptocurrency for the decryption key. Which control is most important in limiting the damage from this type of attack?

options.A: Regular, tested backups stored separately from the production network
options.B: Increasing the internet bandwidth available to the company
options.C: Moving all files to employees' personal laptops
options.D: Disabling the company's firewall to speed up recovery

questions.explanation: This is a ransomware attack. Secure, isolated and regularly tested backups allow the company to restore its data without paying the ransom. Prevention also relies on patching, user training and endpoint protection.

questions.question_text: Within a data governance program, who is typically responsible for defining and maintaining the quality, definitions and appropriate use of a particular set of business data?

options.C: The network administrator
options.D: Every user who enters data

questions.explanation: Data stewards are accountable for specific data domains: they set definitions and quality standards, resolve data issues and ensure the data is used appropriately. Data governance assigns these responsibilities formally, alongside policies covering the data life cycle from capture to purging.

questions.question_text: In the context of big data, the characteristic 'velocity' refers to:

options.A: The sheer amount of data stored
options.B: The speed at which data is generated and must be processed
options.C: The variety of formats in which data arrives
options.D: The accuracy and trustworthiness of the data

questions.explanation: The common Vs of big data are volume (amount), velocity (speed of generation and processing), variety (structured, semi-structured and unstructured formats) and veracity (reliability).

questions.question_text: Which type of analytics recommends a course of action, for example by optimizing the delivery schedule that minimizes cost?

options.C: Diagnostic analytics
options.D: Predictive analytics

questions.explanation: Descriptive analytics reports what happened, diagnostic analytics explains why, predictive analytics forecasts what is likely to happen, and prescriptive analytics recommends what should be done, often using optimization or simulation.

questions.question_text: An analyst drills down into sales data to determine why revenue in the western region fell last quarter. This is an example of:

options.C: Predictive analytics
options.D: Descriptive analytics only

questions.explanation: Diagnostic analytics investigates the causes of past outcomes, using techniques such as drill-down, data discovery and correlation analysis. Simply reporting that revenue fell would be descriptive analytics.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the best example of unstructured data?

options.A: A table of invoice numbers, dates and amounts
options.C: Text of customer reviews posted on social media
options.D: A list of employee IDs and pay rates

questions.explanation: Unstructured data does not fit a predefined data model or row-and-column format; examples include free text, emails, images and video. Invoice tables, ledger balances and payroll lists are structured data.

questions.question_text: A regression of monthly utility cost on machine hours has a coefficient of determination (R-squared) of 0.81. What does this indicate?

options.A: Utility cost increases by $0.81 for each additional machine hour
options.B: There is an 81% probability that the regression equation is correct
options.C: 81% of the variation in utility cost is explained by variation in machine hours
options.D: The correlation coefficient between the variables is 0.81

questions.explanation: R-squared measures the proportion of the variation in the dependent variable explained by the independent variable. It is not the slope, not a probability, and the correlation coefficient would be the square root, 0.9 (if the relationship is positive).

questions.question_text: For a regression model, the total sum of squares is 50,000 and the sum of squared errors (residual sum of squares) is 8,000. What is the coefficient of determination?
questions.explanation: R-squared = 1 - SSE / SST = 1 - 8,000 / 50,000 = 1 - 0.16 = 0.84. So 84% of the variation in the dependent variable is explained by the model. 0.16 is the unexplained proportion, and 0.92 would be the correlation coefficient.

questions.question_text: In a regression of delivery cost on miles driven, the slope coefficient is 3.6 and its standard error is 1.2. Using the common rule of thumb, what can be concluded?

options.A: The t-statistic is 0.33, so miles driven is not statistically significant
options.B: The t-statistic is 4.32, so miles driven explains 43% of delivery cost
options.C: The t-statistic is 3.0, which exceeds 2, so miles driven is a statistically significant explanatory variable
options.D: The t-statistic is 2.4, so the intercept should be removed from the model

questions.explanation: The t-statistic = coefficient / standard error = 3.6 / 1.2 = 3.0. A t-value greater than about 2 indicates that the coefficient is significantly different from zero at roughly the 95% confidence level, so the independent variable has explanatory power.

questions.question_text: A cost estimation equation was derived from data on production between 2,000 and 6,000 units per month. Why should managers be cautious about using it to predict costs at 12,000 units?

options.A: Regression equations can only be used for historical data, never for forecasts
options.B: The intercept automatically becomes negative above the observed range
options.C: The prediction lies outside the relevant range, where the cost relationship may not hold
options.D: R-squared always falls to zero outside the observed data

questions.explanation: Regression results are reliable only within the relevant range of the data used to estimate them. Extrapolating far beyond that range is risky because fixed costs may step up and variable cost rates may change, for example through overtime or capacity constraints.

questions.question_text: What distinguishes Monte Carlo simulation from simple sensitivity analysis?

options.A: It changes one input at a time while holding all others constant
options.B: It repeatedly draws random values for several uncertain inputs from probability distributions to produce a distribution of possible outcomes
options.C: It uses only the single most likely value for each input
options.D: It finds the line of best fit between two variables

questions.explanation: Monte Carlo simulation runs many trials, each using randomly generated values for the uncertain variables based on their probability distributions. The result is a range of outcomes with associated probabilities, rather than a single point estimate.

questions.question_text: An analyst wants to show whether there is a relationship between monthly advertising spend and monthly sales revenue across 36 months. Which visualization is most appropriate?

options.B: A stacked bar chart of sales by product
options.C: A single gauge (dial) chart
options.D: A scatter plot

questions.explanation: A scatter plot shows each observation as a point plotted against two variables, making correlation, clusters and outliers easy to see. Pie charts show composition of a whole, and gauges display a single measure against a target.

questions.question_text: A retailer wants to group its customers into segments based on purchasing behavior, without any predefined labels for the groups. Which data mining technique is most suitable?

options.C: Classification using a labeled training set
options.D: Time-series smoothing

questions.explanation: Clustering is an unsupervised learning technique that groups observations by similarity without predefined categories. Classification is supervised and requires labeled examples, and regression predicts a continuous outcome.

questions.question_text: A company uses exponential smoothing with a smoothing constant (alpha) of 0.3. The forecast for May was 500 units and actual May demand was 540 units. What is the forecast for June?

options.C: 162 units
options.D: 512 units

questions.explanation: New forecast = previous forecast + alpha x (actual - previous forecast) = 500 + 0.3 x (540 - 500) = 500 + 12 = 512 units. Equivalently, 0.3 x 540 + 0.7 x 500.
